name: Natural-rights libertarianism
summary: Natural-rights libertarianism holds that every person owns themselves and that initiating force or fraud against a person or their legitimately acquired property is always wrong, whatever the consequences. From this it derives strong private property rights, rejection of taxation and redistribution as coercion, and wide personal freedom in speech, drugs and consensual conduct. Its adherents divide between anarcho-capitalists who would replace the state with private providers and minarchists who accept a minimal night-watchman state.
scope: The deontological strand of right-libertarianism descended from Locke and developed by Murray Rothbard (The Ethics of Liberty) and Robert Nozick, as applied in the US Libertarian Party platform. It excludes consequentialist libertarianism (Hayek, Friedman), Randian Objectivism, which rests on egoism, and left-libertarianism. Adherents split between anarcho-capitalism and minarchism, so statements about the state itself are answered as split.

keyFigures.name: Murray Rothbard
keyFigures.role: Derived a libertarian legal order from self-ownership and natural law and advocated anarcho-capitalism.

keyFigures.name: Robert Nozick
keyFigures.role: Defended a minimal state grounded in individual rights as side-constraints in Anarchy, State, and Utopia.

sources.author: Murray N. Rothbard
sources.usedFor: Natural law and natural rights from the nature of man, self-ownership and homesteading, land titles, punishment and proportionality, children, immigration, conscription, foreign aid and non-intervention, secession, Berlin on negative freedom.

sources.title: Libertarianism (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

sources.title: Libertarian Party Platform
sources.author: Libertarian Party (United States)
sources.usedFor: Applied policy positions: drugs, speech, guns, taxes, welfare, immigration, conscription, alliances, discrimination, property and pollution, banking.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Redistribution through the state is rejected and no one has an enforceable duty to aid others, so tax-funded guaranteed care violates rights; care is left to private and voluntary provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A wage floor overrides voluntary exchange between employer and worker, which Rothbard treats as the paradigm of legitimate interaction, and the party platform opposes government controls on property and contract.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Right-libertarians back free-market capitalism and the platform calls for removing government barriers to trade, though the case is primarily about rights rather than efficiency.

public-ownership.rationale: Government takeover of industries rests on taxation and monopoly privilege, which Rothbard calls invasions of property; the platform favours private ownership and market provision.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: All redistributive taxation is rejected and the platform opposes any tax increase for any reason, so higher rates on anyone are wrong.

unions-good.rationale: Voluntary unions are legitimate exercises of association but libertarians are split on whether unions are beneficial, and coercive privileges are rejected; the sources do not rate unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property in oneself and in homesteaded resources is the foundation of the whole system: Rothbard deduces all rights from it and treats any interference as invasion.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Government intervention in markets is seen as coercive, and the platform wants owners free of government controls on the use of their property.

cut-welfare.rationale: State welfare is rejected as a rights violation and the platform phases out Social Security and public aid in favour of voluntary help; the dependency argument is secondary to the rights argument.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers may voluntarily form cooperatives, but nothing in the theory says they should; ownership follows homesteading and contract, so an obligation to collective ownership is rejected.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Rights act as side-constraints that hold regardless of consequences, so security benefits do not justify state intrusion on persons and property.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The platform calls for repeal of laws against drug use for medicinal or recreational purposes as crimes without victims, and the tradition opposes laws against consensual adult conduct.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The platform opposes government censorship and states that offensive language is not grounds for legal action.

strong-leader.rationale: Concentrated unchecked executive power is the state apparatus Rothbard sees as predatory; the tradition seeks to limit and shrink political power, not to free it from checks.

state-harmful.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists such as Rothbard call the state an institutionalised aggressor, whereas minarchists such as Nozick defend a minimal state, so adherents are split.

limit-guns.rationale: The platform affirms the right to keep and bear arms and opposes laws restricting, registering or monitoring firearms.

empower-police-military.rationale: The platform backs a military sufficient to defend the country but opposes qualified immunity and foreign intervention, so more funding and authority for state forces is not wanted.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Consensual adult exchange is a victimless act under the platform's repeal of victimless-crime laws and the self-ownership principle, though sex work is not named in the pages read.

decide-locally.rationale: Rothbard's reasoning on secession runs down to ever smaller units, favouring decentralised authority, though the core aim is protecting rights rather than localism as such.

rehabilitation.rationale: Rothbard builds punishment on proportionality and restitution to the victim, not on reform of the offender.

traditional-family.rationale: The platform says government should not define or license personal relationships; as a social claim about families the ideology is indifferent.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The platform holds government should not license relationships but, while licenses exist, they must go to all consenting adults who apply.

abortion-legal.rationale: Self-ownership is said to ground a woman's right to end an unwanted pregnancy and Rothbard defends an eviction right, though some libertarians who treat the fetus as a person dissent.

more-religion-public.rationale: Libertarianism limits the state's role, so state promotion of religion is unwelcome though private religious life is protected; the sources give no direct position.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Rothbard supports restitution to identifiable victims of land theft and rejects titles rooted in aggression, but not collective state programmes funded by taxation.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The ideology takes no position on this empirical question, so the answer is an inference of indifference.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Culture is left to voluntary association; the sources show no stance on the importance of national tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Rothbard seeks radical principled change but through peaceful means; the sources do not endorse gradualism as such, so adherents are split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The platform calls for unrestricted movement of people across borders and Rothbard argues immigration barriers restrict property owners' rights, though Hoppe's strand differs.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: More power to supranational bodies enlarges state coercion and the platform rejects entangling foreign commitments.

free-trade.rationale: The platform supports removing governmental barriers to trade and opposes tariffs, though the justification is rights-based rather than a long-run benefits claim.

nation-first.rationale: The platform wants non-intervention but also free trade and open movement, so neither national self-assertion nor global state cooperation fits; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Rothbard advocates non-intervention among states and the platform rejects foreign intervention; military action funded by taxes and conscription violates rights.

open-borders.rationale: The platform backs unrestricted movement of people across borders, but Rothbard ties immigration to private property so the answer is not unqualified.

limit-growth.rationale: Free-market capitalism is central and no collective limit on production is justified without a rights violation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The platform relies on property rights and court-enforced restitution for proven harm rather than government regulation.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: An optimism about markets and innovation is common among adherents but the sources do not state it as doctrine; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Absent specific stance, opposing government controls on property use and energy would favour allowing nuclear power; inferred and subsidy views vary.

revolution-justified.rationale: Force is justified to stop rights violations, which in the Lockean tradition extends to resisting tyranny, though the sources stress peaceful change.

experts-over-public.rationale: The tradition distrusts concentrated political authority and treats individual rights, not expert judgment, as the guide to law.

central-planning.rationale: Economic intervention is seen as coercive and counterproductive; libertarians favour laissez-faire.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public ownership is rejected as coercive and worker ownership is merely permissible, so conditioning markets on either is not accepted.

land-value-tax.rationale: A land tax is still taxation, rejected as theft; the SEP associates land taxes with left-libertarians who reject the right-libertarian view of appropriation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Transfers by gift and bequest are legitimate holdings under the entitlement view, and taxing them is taxation the party wants ended.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional state payment is redistribution funded by taxation, which is rejected; the party wants help to come from voluntary efforts.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The platform rejects tariffs and supports removing barriers to trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of capital is intervention in markets and the platform opposes bailouts and manipulation of money and credit.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Right-libertarians accept any distribution that arises through just acquisition and exchange and impose no quantitative limit, so engineering wide ownership is not a goal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Voluntary exchange and contract, including wage contracts, are central to Rothbard's theory of liberty.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The platform backs free-market banking and opposes inflationary monetary policy, which leans toward ending central banking, but the page does not call for abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices override voluntary contract and exchange.

one-party-rule.rationale: The platform defends free speech, due process and limits on government; single-party control contradicts it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Libertarians doubt that any state, hereditary or elected, holds inherent authority, though some adherents favour monarchy as the lesser evil; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy is valued instrumentally for limiting state power but is not seen as conferring legitimacy, and voter ignorance and public choice are cited against it.

direct-votes.rationale: Majority votes cannot override rights, so extending direct voting does not advance the core aim; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of political power replace individual rights with collective rule.

right-to-secede.rationale: Rothbard argues that once any right of secession is admitted there is no stopping point short of individual secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Self-ownership gives everyone equal standing and rules out claims of natural entitlement to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Force is justified to prevent or answer rights violations, including self-defence, so a blanket ban is not accepted.

war-builds-character.rationale: Rothbard treats war as the state's gravest crime, financed by tax aggression and conscription.

separate-church-state.rationale: A limited government has no business imposing or funding religion and the platform defends individual choice, though the strictness of separation is not detailed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rothbard grounds law in natural law known by reason, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists such as Rothbard want private provision of courts, police and defence while Nozick holds a minimal state emerges from protective agencies, so adherents mostly accept private provision as possible.

military-superiority.rationale: The platform backs only a military sufficient for defence and Rothbard condemns imperialism and war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rights belong to individuals regardless of ethnicity, so an ethnic definition of the nation has no standing.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rothbard sees a conflict between the state's ruling class and the producers but not the Marxist economic class conflict; typical adherents reject the claim as stated.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The SEP states that distributive justice is historical, so patterns of outcomes do not matter.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Rothbard bases land titles on homesteading and restitution to identifiable victims, not on collective authority of a people over territory; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Rectification goes to actual victims from actual aggressors; payments from present taxpayers would be a fresh aggression.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political unions among states enlarge state power and are not grounded in individual consent.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rand's rational egoism affirms it, but the deontological rights tradition rests on rights as constraints and not on egoism, so adherents are split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights are treated as side-constraints, prior to any community claim.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Rothbard denies rights to animals but the doctrine does not address intrinsic natural value; inferred indifference.

limit-population.rationale: Coercive limits on reproduction violate self-ownership.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Capitalism and its productive growth are defended as beneficial.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Adherents generally welcome innovation but would not impose disruption through state action; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Strong rights of control over one's own body and the platform's view that people decide what they knowingly consume support freedom to modify oneself.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Ceding government decisions to algorithms increases rather than shrinks state power; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Peaceful private communication is a person's own property and no state claim overrides it; inferred from self-ownership.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology is principle-driven and doesn't value restoration of past orders as such; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Natural-rights libertarianism holds rights as side-constraints regardless of consequences, opposing a purely results-based test.

direct-action.rationale: The party pursues change through elections, education and defence of rights; the sources do not address direct action as method.

means-match-ends.rationale: Non-aggression applies to methods as well as aims, so coercive means are barred; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Capitalism and productive exchange are defended.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rothbard builds on voluntary exchange among specialised producers.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution follows just holdings, not need, and there is no enforceable duty to aid.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profits from legitimately acquired property and voluntary contract are not coercive.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorial rule over a class violates equal rights and due process.

collective-farming.rationale: Land belongs to those who homestead and transform it, not to collectives imposed by the state.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rothbard attributes war to states and their taxation and conscription, not to markets.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxation is called theft in the tradition: the SEP compares redistributive taxation with forced labour and the platform seeks to end all taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Force is justified to prevent violations of rights, which is narrower than harm in general but broadly parallel.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights belong to individuals, especially self-ownership, and group rights are treated as claims of individuals only.

conscription.rationale: The platform opposes any form of compulsory national service and Rothbard calls conscription slavery by the state.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Adherents prize freedom to leave and distrust majority voting, but the sources do not rank them explicitly; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Competition among jurisdictions appeals to some adherents but anarchists reject any state; inferred split.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rothbard defines liberty as absence of interference and says positive liberty is not liberty at all, praising Berlin's negative freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Rothbard stresses court intellectuals' role in legitimising the state, but the claim about relative power is not part of the doctrine; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The ideology holds individuals have equal rights regardless of ability and does not take a view on this empirical claim.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through compulsory bodies conflicts with individual consent and association.

total-state.rationale: State direction of all life is the opposite of the limited state or no state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Collective national projects are a state aim, not a libertarian one.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Rothbard condemns imperialism and any state aggression abroad.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on oaths of lordship and bound followers is feudal aggression Rothbard counts as invalid titles.

bound-labor.rationale: Rothbard considers feudal bonds ethically invalid and holds that self-ownership cannot be alienated into permanent servitude.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Rothbard holds that reason can discover objective natural law and the nature of man.

universal-morality.rationale: Rothbard argues natural law is discoverable by reason from the nature of man and holds for all people.

single-common-good.rationale: Aggregate or collective goods do not justify overriding individual rights, which are side-constraints.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Natural-rights libertarians judge states by their respect for individual rights rather than by national claims, and the sources give no position on this case.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Rothbard says there can be no human right to immigrate because it would be a claim on someone else's property, so a group right of return is not recognised.

revive-national-language.rationale: Imposing a language through the state would be coercion funded by taxes.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Owners decide how their property is run and others have no claim to a vote absent contract.

school-vouchers.rationale: The platform wants parents to control education funds and market provision, so vouchers are a partial step, though public funding itself is objectionable.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The platform opposes bailouts, inflationary monetary policy and tax increases, which points against deficit stimulus.

economic-freedom.rationale: Property rights are the basis of freedom and economic and political liberty are treated as one set of rights.

rule-by-example.rationale: The platform favours limits on government through law and due process rather than reliance on rulers' virtue; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Rothbard's secession reasoning supports groups governing themselves, though his ultimate unit is the individual.

force-without-un.rationale: The platform rejects foreign intervention whether or not a UN body approves it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rothbard grounds ethics in reason, though religious libertarians exist.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The platform wants welfare ended altogether, so the question of who qualifies is not addressed; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The platform rejects state welfare and offers no view on conditions for it; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Voluntary exchange is mutually beneficial and the doctrine does not see employers and workers as opposed classes; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nothing in the theory justifies coercive destruction of property or institutions; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: States forming blocs is not a libertarian goal and Rothbard opposes alliances and conflict between states; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: The class-based framework is not accepted and the doctrine is individualist; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The platform states government should not discriminate by sex and equal rights hold before the law.

ban-interest.rationale: Voluntary exchange and contract are central and lending at interest harms no one's rights.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The platform says government should not discriminate on ethnicity, so law-mandated segregation is rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rothbard describes the state as a monopoly privileged to invade property and its ideologists as justifiers of its crimes, though he does not use Marxist class analysis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Owners should be free to use their property without government controls, favouring producers; subsidies are opposed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Coercive assimilation is not libertarian and the doctrine leaves culture to private associations; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: The ideology has no such conspiracy claim and treats immigration as individual and property choices; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Libertarians doubt democracy confers legitimacy and take no view on seat allocation; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a form of government abroad is intervention that Rothbard and the platform reject.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The doctrine is individualist and not committed to systemic claims, though law should treat the sexes equally; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Public-choice reasoning cited in the SEP and Rothbard's critique of the state as predatory support the claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Self-ownership rules out forced restrictions on reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The platform calls for ending qualified immunity so officers can be held accountable.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Nozick and minarchists endorse this limit while anarcho-capitalists would go further, so most adherents agree with the limit as a ceiling.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The ideology holds equal individual rights and leaves family choices free.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rights belong to every individual equally and the platform opposes government discrimination.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The question is internal to Marxism and the ideology has no position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Rothbard judges land titles by homesteading and aggression and offers no general verdict on settler states; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal treatment before the law fits the platform's rule-of-law position, though private legal systems are also favoured; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The platform defends individual freedom of conscience and opposes such restrictions.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Rothbard rejects animal rights and holds that law should punish only aggression against persons and property.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Libertarians would privatise schooling, but state schools while they exist should not impose religion; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The doctrine wants the state reduced or limited, not strengthened.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The SEP notes strong scepticism of state legitimacy, so authority without individual consent is illegitimate.

trade-surplus.rationale: Free trade is supported and no state target for export surpluses is justified.

population-transfer.rationale: Rothbard's non-aggression principle forbids coercion of peaceful persons, which excludes forcing a minority out; transfers as such are not discussed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Competition in markets is favoured but the claim about struggle between peoples is not part of the doctrine; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The platform opposes censorship and abridgment of speech and association.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Rothbard defines liberty as absence of interference, so mere power to interfere does not remove freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Limiting concentrated power is consistent with the doctrine though Rothbard doubted constitutional checks; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: A party directing the working class conflicts with individual freedom and voluntary association.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Law protects rights equally and does not prioritise groups by need.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Privatisation of public housing is consistent with the platform, though state property transfers raise questions; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voluntary strikes are permitted but government regulation of unions and picketing is intervention; owners may exclude pickets from their property.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The doctrine blames state interference rather than population for poverty; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The doctrine is individualist and treats voluntary association as the basis of society; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lotteries do not address legitimacy of political power; the doctrine seeks fewer offices; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The platform defends due process, jury trials and the presumption of innocence.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The platform wants property owners free of government controls and opposes interference in markets.

party-controls-media.rationale: The platform opposes government censorship of speech and press.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party controlling the military contradicts limits on government and defence of rights.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The platform backs unrestricted movement of people, so long waits for citizenship are not favoured; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The doctrine has no position on pay levels; it wants far less government; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Individual conscience is prized, but internal party rules are private matters; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Larger supranational states enlarge coercion, though removing trade barriers is welcome.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The doctrine does not address the allocation of command powers within a state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Churches are private associations free to organise as members choose.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clergy has no basis in consent or rights and imposes religious law by force.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rothbard strongly opposes war but the doctrine does not endorse working for defeat as a method; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The platform opposes government censorship of speech and the press.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The doctrine seeks limits on political power, so unlimited terms are not favoured; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Mechanisms making officials answerable fit the doctrine's distrust of political power; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The platform rejects entangling alliances and foreign intervention.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Owners may let property by contract and the platform wants property owners free from government controls.

people-in-arms.rationale: The platform backs a defensive military and private gun rights but takes no stand on replacing the army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: A cultural claim on which the doctrine is indifferent.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The doctrine decides by consent and individual rights, with no view on reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: A sociological claim on which the doctrine is indifferent.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Rothbard asserts universal ethics but says nothing on ranking cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: The platform opposes state executions; Rothbard would allow capital punishment only for murder and only under a proportionality limit.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Libertarians would end state control of curricula and leave content to parents and schools; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: State-imposed curricula of any kind are rejected in favour of market provision; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The platform opposes government censorship and treats victimless acts as outside the law.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The doctrine focuses on individual rights and takes no position on state rules for citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Tax-funded language programmes rely on taxation, which is rejected.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Libertarians favour repealing burdensome laws for everyone rather than granting group exemptions; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Individual liberty is prized, though the doctrine concerns state coercion and not social pressure; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: State debts are burdens on taxpayers, and cancelling them is consistent with rejecting tax aggression; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The doctrine treats political and economic liberty as one but not that independence requires transformation; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The doctrine is sceptical of democratic legitimacy and takes no view on constitution-making procedure.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty is a right and not a trade-off against growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Rothbard calls for rigorous abstention from foreign aid and the SEP notes no enforceable duty to aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The platform backs defence only and rejects foreign entanglements, but supports weapons for defence; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The doctrine takes no position on election methods.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The platform seeks free-market banking and a halt to inflationary policy, not a more independent central bank.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Homesteading and just titles decide claims, with no general rule on peace agreements.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property rights follow from self-ownership and homesteading and do not depend on any common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The question is internal to socialist debate, and the doctrine does not address it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The platform requires proven damage for restitution, and rejects regulation based on uncertain harm.

collective-defense.rationale: The platform rejects entangling alliances and foreign intervention.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The doctrine judges by individual consent and titles and has no stated rule on annexations.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: State control of religious institutions violates freedom of conscience and property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A constitutional design question the doctrine does not address.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Rothbard accepts a right of secession down to the individual.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Voluntary differing arrangements and decentralisation are consistent with Rothbard on secession; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rothbard rejects claims of special status for the state and its ideologists.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The platform seeks to end income tax entirely and opposes any increase; a flat rate would be a lesser evil, so adherents are split.

character-from-environment.rationale: The ideology emphasises individual responsibility but takes no stand on the sources of character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The platform requires due process and limits on rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Expansion by private enterprise is consistent with the ideology but it is not a doctrinal goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: A design question outside the core doctrine, which doubts democracy and favours limits on power.

leader-cult.rationale: Rothbard criticises ideologists who justify the state by exalting it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Rothbard treats parents as guardians and the doctrine has no view on custody presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Internal to Marxist debate and outside the doctrine.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rothbard holds that feudal and engrossed land titles are invalid and the land belongs to those transforming it, but legitimate estates are protected.

refugee-return.rationale: Rothbard supports restitution to proven victims of land theft but the sources do not address descendants of refugees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territory is held by individual title and not by nationality of the people living there.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The platform's defence of freedom of conscience and its opposition to laws against victimless conduct rule out punishing apostasy; apostasy is not named.

women-must-cover.rationale: The platform holds that people should be free to make personal choices that harm no one else and opposes laws on victimless conduct, which rules out a legal dress code; dress is not named.

common-currency.rationale: The platform backs market money and the doctrine is indifferent on shared currencies; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political unions based on ancestry have no basis in the doctrine's individual consent.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Voluntary association is fine but the doctrine does not address minority self-government.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The doctrine holds that rights apply to individuals anywhere and does not rank staying over emigrating.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rothbard stresses ideas and the nature of man in shaping law and society, and the sources do not endorse economic determinism; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Intervention in markets is seen as coercive, and without state privilege cartels are left to voluntary competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: The platform states opposition to bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rights are side-constraints that majorities may not override, so courts enforcing them may constrain majority will.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Required quotas conflict with equal treatment and the platform's opposition to government discrimination.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The platform supports free trade and open movement of capital.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade agreements are government controls, whereas the platform favours removing barriers to trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Voluntary exchange for material gain is the model of free interaction.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Force is justified only against rights violations, and the sources do not endorse vanguard armed action; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Legal privileges conferred by the state are invalid, though inheritance of property is legitimate; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rothbard condemns imperialism as aggression by states.

patriotic-education.rationale: State-directed education promoting loyalty conflicts with market provision of education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The platform holds that government should not discriminate by ethnicity or sex.

public-money-creation.rationale: The platform favours free-market banking and opposes inflationary government money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Adherents see crises as caused by state intervention and not by capitalism itself; the sources do not state the claim directly.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The platform rejects foreign intervention and entangling relationships.

delink-world-market.rationale: The platform supports free trade and free movement of capital.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Workers' gains arise from voluntary exchange and not extraction from poor countries; the doctrine rejects the extraction claim.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The platform lets private organisations set their own membership standards, and property rights imply the same for owners.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Written limits on government power fit the platform's defence of rights, though Rothbard doubted constitutions' effectiveness.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The doctrine has no stated position on colonial treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The doctrine doubts that elections confer legitimacy and has no preference among rulers' selection.

minority-veto.rationale: Rothbard's logic of secession down to the individual means no decision binds a dissenter without consent, though practical limits are accepted.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Force is justified to defend rights, and the Lockean tradition allows resisting rulers who violate them.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Legislatures should be limited by rights, so no body should be supreme; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Rothbard denies that animals have rights but does not deny that their suffering matters; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Rothbard holds that people may kill and eat animals and, as property owners, use them, while humane treatment is a moral rather than legal matter.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity is praised but cannot be compelled, so it is a moral and not a political duty on which adherents split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Some adherents advise withdrawal but the party and movement engage politics, so adherents are split.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critique rooted in Marxist theory that the doctrine does not hold; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Rothbard says statist ideologists persuade the public to accept the state's crimes, which fits this claim; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Trade is mutually beneficial and the doctrine rejects extraction explanations.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist question outside the doctrine.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Rothbard opposes foreign aid but supports trade and capital flows, so the statement's rejection of investment is not shared.

return-lost-territory.rationale: State claims to territory do not follow from the doctrine, which focuses on individual titles.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Political rule by descent conflicts with equal individual rights.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: A constitutional design question outside the doctrine.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Both are seen as extreme state coercion, but the sources do not address the comparison.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical dispute on which adherents are split and which the doctrine does not settle.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The doctrine has no stance on public monuments, though it opposes state expenditure generally.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The doctrine is indifferent on targeted programmes while opposing state programmes generally.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Violence against any person is aggression under the non-aggression principle, whoever commits it; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rothbard bases rights on universal natural law, so the claim that institutions suit only some civilizations is rejected.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military political power contradicts limits on government and the platform's defence-only military.

paid-care-work.rationale: Public payment relies on taxation and wages arise from voluntary exchange.

filial-duty.rationale: A moral matter with no enforceable duties, on which the doctrine is silent.

office-by-exam.rationale: A civil service design question the doctrine does not address.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The platform supports free movement of financial capital across borders.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The platform holds government should not define or license relationships, so marriage ends by agreement.

recallable-delegates.rationale: A representation question the doctrine does not address.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The platform phases out Social Security in favour of private voluntary systems.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land is owned by those who homestead and transform it, and title is not conditional on continued use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Limiting executive power over money is consistent with the doctrine; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Imposing a language through the state is coercion.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Owners may sell to anyone and the platform favours free movement of capital.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Liability without intent contradicts rule-of-law and property-rights principles, and the platform holds government should not discriminate.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Voluntary consumption is each person's choice and the doctrine would not call it harmful.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The platform rejects foreign intervention and sanctions.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Rothbard calls for non-intervention among states.

corporate-influence.rationale: Public-choice reasoning implies corporations use political power to gain privileges, a view libertarians share.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The platform opposes government censorship and abridgment of speech and association.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Tax-funded incentives are redistribution and rejected.

residents-only-property.rationale: Owners hold rights to sell and rent to anyone, as Rothbard argues in the case of immigration barriers.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state-funded job guarantee is redistribution and compelled employment funded by taxation.

democratic-peace.rationale: The doctrine opposes spreading regimes by force, and sources do not endorse the premise.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The SEP notes strong scepticism of state legitimacy and philosophical anarchism is common.

non-intervention.rationale: Rothbard states a libertarian policy of peaceful coexistence and non-intervention between states.

industrial-unions.rationale: A union organisation question the doctrine leaves to voluntary choice.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The doctrine treats persons as individuals with equal rights and has no ethnic conspiracy claims.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The platform holds that government should not define, license or restrict personal relationships.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency limits government power and fits the doctrine; inferred.

local-production.rationale: The platform favours free trade, and no state preference for local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: A method question the doctrine does not address.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The platform rejects international control but the doctrine does not rank legal orders.

religious-nation.rationale: A nation defined by religion contradicts individual rights and freedom of conscience.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The platform rejects entangling alliances and dominance by powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Smaller political units are favoured by Rothbard's reasoning on secession; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Rothbard holds that property rights extend to all justly acquired goods, including means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rothbard advocates peaceful coexistence and non-intervention between states, not wars to defeat regimes.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public funding remains taxation, though private delivery is a step toward the platform's goal.

religion-illusion.rationale: A theological question outside the doctrine, with religious and atheist libertarians.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Right-libertarians defend free-market capitalism and its productive results.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The platform holds equal rights suffice and rejects transforming the economy by state action.

socialized-care.rationale: Public services rest on taxation, and family choices are private.

purge-loanwords.rationale: State language regulation is coercion against free speech.

treaties-binding.rationale: The doctrine bases rights on individual titles and has no stated view on treaties with nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary communes are permitted but the doctrine does not call for reorganising society into them; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-organised settlement programmes are coercive and use taxes.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Rothbard bases land title on homesteading and transformation, not historical or religious ties.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The doctrine does not address this historical question and adherents overwhelmingly reject denial; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The platform opposes laws on victimless conduct and holds government should not restrict personal relationships.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The platform defends free speech and due process.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The platform opposes government censorship and speech restrictions.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Rothbard condemns imperialism as state aggression.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious obligation the doctrine neither endorses nor addresses.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A religious test for rulers has no basis in consent or rights.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The doctrine doubts democracy as a source of legitimacy and favours voluntary association; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The doctrine is individualist and rejects group-based oppression analysis; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The platform opposes government discrimination and favours individual choice; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: The platform holds that individuals decide what risks they accept with their own bodies.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Rothbard framed the issue as liberty versus the state, but the doctrine takes no position on the statement.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist theory of alienation is not accepted and voluntary exchange is defended.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The doctrine treats individuals as bearers of equal rights regardless of religion.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Rothbard grounds natural law in reason and the nature of man, not divine command.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The platform defends individual conduct and conscience, so restrictions on dress by students are rejected.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Contracts freely made are enforced under Rothbard's theory of contract.

social-market-economy.rationale: Right-libertarians favour laissez-faire over social protection by the state.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The platform backs a defensive military and minarchists keep state forces, though anarchists would privatise defence.

rich-first.rationale: No permission from the state is needed for individuals to prosper, though the doctrine does not address regional sequencing; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The doctrine doubts any state's authority and does not rank succession methods.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Voluntary lending at interest is legitimate, though user-owned banks are permitted.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The platform opposes the international lenders but supports spending restraint, so adherents mix.

property-franchise.rationale: Libertarians favour equal rights and doubt democracy's legitimacy, though some historic thinkers favoured a property franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: A feminist ecological theory the doctrine does not hold; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist theory the doctrine does not hold; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Property rights in presses and halls are legitimate, and free speech is protected.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The platform defends due process and rule of law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The platform opposes government discrimination on ethnicity and holds equal rights.

online-participation.rationale: A mechanism question outside the doctrine.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Government should not define or restrict personal relationships among consenting adults.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Rothbard holds that boycotts are legitimate whatever their purpose, but whether people should boycott a minority is a different question the doctrine would answer no.

citizens-assembly.rationale: A democratic mechanism and the doctrine doubts democracy as a source of authority; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: An internal religious matter outside the doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Right-libertarians do not oppose concentrations of economic power that arise by non-coercive means.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The platform holds that government should not discriminate by sexual orientation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The platform defends freedom of conscience and opposes state propaganda.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists would replace state police with private providers while minarchists keep them, so adherents split.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The doctrine takes individual rights as the basis and doubts group-based power arrangements; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The platform states that help for the poor should come from voluntary efforts of private groups.

term-limits.rationale: Limits on political tenure fit the doctrine's distrust of power; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: A mechanism question outside the doctrine.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The doctrine is silent on public policy priorities of this kind.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious bodies are private associations free to set their own rules.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marriage is a private contract and equal rights are held, but the doctrine lets spouses decide.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: A franchise question outside the doctrine.

rent-control.rationale: The platform wants property owners free from government controls on the use of their property.

abolish-ip.rationale: Rothbard distinguishes patents from copyrights and others reject all intellectual property, so adherents are split.

uniformed-youth.rationale: State-organised drilled youth movements are coercive and use taxes.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The doctrine has no stated position on basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The platform rejects entangling alliances and calls for non-intervention abroad.

recognise-genocide.rationale: A symbolic act of governments on which the doctrine has no position.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Just holdings, including returns on property, are legitimate under the entitlement theory.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Rothbard holds that a person may defend himself and may employ or accept help from others in doing so.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: A historical claim on which the doctrine is silent.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The doctrine takes no position on this theoretical question.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: An internal feminist debate outside the doctrine.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The doctrine rejects state cults of the nation; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics is understood as the protection of rights, not as a metaphysical contest.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A national question the doctrine does not address.

culture-before-state.rationale: The doctrine has no position on cultural sequencing.

god-not-male.rationale: A theological question outside the doctrine.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A theological question outside the doctrine.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ownership by ethnic criteria contradicts free exchange and equal rights.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The doctrine does not address administrative boundaries beyond secession.

independent-unions.rationale: Voluntary organisations free of the state fit the doctrine's association principle; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: An internal socialist debate outside the doctrine.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of services relies on taxation and the platform favours market provision.

second-chamber.rationale: A constitutional design question the doctrine does not address.

municipal-property.rationale: Property is held by individuals through homesteading and exchange, not by communities or states.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Voluntary confederation is permissible but the doctrine is not committed to it; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Wages arise from voluntary contract and not from legal family-support requirements.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Regulation of medical products is government intervention and the platform wants owners free from such controls.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Public funding relies on taxation, though private research is welcome.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Peaceful voluntary exchange is outside legitimate state interference and the platform favours free-market money; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Peaceful speech and association need no identification; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: The SEP says force is justified only to prevent rights violations and not to serve others' good, and rights act as side-constraints on any community end.

spiritual-nature.rationale: A metaphysical question outside the doctrine.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Rothbard's reasoning on secession favours decentralisation and not revocable powers; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Owners should be free to use technology without government controls; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: The doctrine is indifferent on urban form beyond property rights.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Rights belong to individuals and not to racial groups.

racial-pride.rationale: The doctrine does not address this personal attitude.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The platform backs a military sufficient to defend and opposes foreign intervention.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The doctrine is individualist and does not define nations by language; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate electorates by religion treat people as group members and not equal individuals.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A conspiracy claim the doctrine does not hold; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Tax-funded tuition is redistribution, and the platform favours market provision of education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The platform favours court-enforced restitution for proven damages over taxes and regulation.

future-generations.rationale: The doctrine does not address obligations across generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The doctrine is individualist and rejects group character claims; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: A limited defensive military follows from the platform; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: The platform calls for unrestricted movement of financial capital across borders.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The platform opposes laws restricting private firearms and the doctrine favours private defence.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Rothbard condemns war but defence is legitimate, so adherents split on a general duty of refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Voluntary bargaining is permitted but the doctrine favours individual freedom of contract; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are redistribution and rejected.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The platform opposes high spending and inflationary policy; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The platform seeks free trade and not managed economic rules favouring particular countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists would abolish the state and minarchists would limit it, so adherents split on the Marxist framing.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Voluntary communities with different arrangements fit the doctrine, though it holds a fixed set of rights; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Private ownership of resources is favoured as a way to avoid the tragedy of the commons; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Collective national sanctity is not a basis for rights.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Cancelling debts at taxpayer expense is redistribution.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The doctrine rejects exploitation frameworks of this kind; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rothbard grounds natural law and natural rights in the nature of man, which is the basis of dignity and rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Public funding of media relies on taxation and the platform opposes government involvement in speech.

religions-one-truth.rationale: A theological question outside the doctrine.

farm-price-support.rationale: The platform opposes government controls and subsidies in markets.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The platform backs defence but the doctrine is split between defence needs and disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: The doctrine has no position on party strategy.

ban-fgm.rationale: Rothbard says parents may not aggress against children, and cutting a child is aggression.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Rights belong to every individual equally, including property rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic question outside the doctrine.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The platform relies on property rights and court-enforced restitution for proven damages.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: A formal official role for hereditary or customary bodies conflicts with individual consent.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Rights are side-constraints that regulation cannot override.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Rothbard bases punishment on proportionality to the offence and the victim's claims, not legislated minima.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The platform backs unrestricted movement and the doctrine opposes state mandates on language.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Compulsion to join or pay violates freedom of association and contract.

voter-id.rationale: An electoral administration question the doctrine does not address.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The state should not favour any interpretation, as the platform defends freedom of conscience; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: A definitional question on which the doctrine has no position.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The platform opposes government censorship and speech restrictions.

premarital-sex.rationale: The platform opposes laws on consensual private conduct, though it takes no moral stance.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Replacing welfare with cash payments is still redistribution through taxation, though a lesser evil than the existing system.

women-suffrage.rationale: Rights belong to individuals equally, though libertarians doubt democracy's role.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The doctrine is individualist and does not hold the claim; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The doctrine takes no position on this empirical question.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Government agencies are funded by taxes and the platform opposes state discrimination programmes.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The non-aggression principle is the defining rule of the tradition: rights act as side-constraints so initiating force or fraud is impermissible regardless of consequences.

history-own-civilization.rationale: State-set curricula are rejected in favour of market provision of education, and the doctrine is universalist about rights; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices by birth contradicts equal rights before the law and the platform opposes government discrimination.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Rothbard grounds all property titles in homesteading of unowned resources and self-ownership, and the SEP notes right-libertarians permit unilateral appropriation without a quantitative limit.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not a settled position; inferred from the stress on non-intervention and doubts about supranational bodies, though leaders who violate rights are guilty.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The ideology takes no stand on religious doctrine; it concerns only coercion between persons.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from its individualism: it rejects group rights and state-imposed arrangements, so mandated guarantees conflict with free association.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Planned economies and state ownership violate property rights and are coercive whoever rules them (s1, s3).

indirect-election.rationale: Adherents are split on democracy and the state, and the question concerns the mechanics of state office.

national-church-status.rationale: A privileged legal status for a church implies state coercion and tax support, which the ideology rejects (s3).

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its support for secession and decentralisation, though it does not treat ethnicity as the basis of rights.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Rothbard supports the right of secession and voluntary association (s1), which supports local choice of jurisdiction.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from its view that legitimate title comes from property, not from the borders of states.

simple-living.rationale: It leaves the pace and style of life to individual choice and values trade and abundance, though it does not oppose simple living by choice.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The ideology favours free movement and exchange, and the platform opposes state limits on settlement (s4).

equal-conscription.rationale: It opposes conscription as slavery, so a draft for neither sex is the position it prefers (s1, s3, s4).

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Libertarianism centres individual rights rather than collective national bonds; rejection is inferred from that individualism, not from a source on nationhood.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Rothbard limits punishment to proportionate response after due determination of guilt, and drug use and sale are victimless acts that the platform would not criminalise at all.

close-ties-china.rationale: The ideology favours free trade with everyone but opposes government-directed alliances; the statement's either-or framing is inferred as neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Using state funds and power to support co-ethnics abroad conflicts with non-intervention and tax rejection; this is inferred from those principles.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Rothbard holds that unowned resources become rightful property by homesteading, with no compensation owed to others, against common-ownership views.

self-ownership.rationale: Self-ownership is the foundational premise of the doctrine, stated directly by Rothbard and described as central in the SEP.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation is treated as coercion, and the platform calls for ending taxes that fund state programmes, so cutting sales taxes is a step toward that.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Adherents reject tax-funded redistribution altogether, so neither universal nor targeted spending is endorsed; a mild disagree is inferred, since minarchists may tolerate minimal targeted aid.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The ideology has no leader-centred populism and the Libertarian Party itself is a party; disagreement is inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Rothbard and the platform oppose subsidies, monopoly grants and corporate favours as state coercion that violates equal rights.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Libertarians favour separation of religion and state and no state-imposed religious structure, though the statement on party organisation is inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Libertarianism leaves the choice of values and technology to individuals and has no collective view; neutrality is inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Equal individual rights and voluntary association imply either spouse may leave a marriage; this is inferred and adherents differ on legal divorce rules.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resources should be privately owned by whoever homesteaded them, not controlled by the nation, but foreign-versus-domestic owners is not discussed, so this is inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Nozick's entitlement theory and Rothbard hold that holdings are just if acquired and transferred without force or fraud, whatever the resulting pattern.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Taxation is regarded as theft and the platform opposes taxes on voluntary exchange, so a levy on financial trades is rejected.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from the view that state intervention and law, not private prejudice, are the chief barriers; the sources do not address this question directly and adherents differ.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The strand is grounded in natural rights above positive law; Rothbard argues that law violating natural law lacks legitimacy, so an unjust statute carries no moral authority.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Adherents welcome technology chosen by free markets but have no stance that society should aim to automate work; the aim is a matter for individuals and the market, and reduced work is not an aim.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed by the theory; non-interventionism opposes a dominant world power, but anarcho-capitalists and minarchists differ on world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Rothbard and the Austrian tradition behind it hold value to be subjective, set by individual valuation and demand, not embodied labour.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from individualism that rejects collective national loyalty as a political basis; the platform's non-interventionism and the movement's hostility to the state weaken patriotism, but it is not stated.

material-over-identity.rationale: The statement concerns the left; libertarians hold that neither wages nor identity should be directed by politics, so the question does not map onto their position.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: One-party socialist rule violates self-ownership and property rights; for this strand markets need free politics and the state's coercive socialism is rejected.

missingStatements.text: The first person to claim and transform an unowned resource thereby becomes its rightful owner.
missingStatements.rationale: Rothbard grounds all property titles in homesteading of unowned resources and self-ownership, and the SEP notes right-libertarians permit unilateral appropriation without a quantitative limit.

missingStatements.text: Punishment of crime should be proportional to the harm done and should aim at restitution to the victim.
missingStatements.rationale: Rothbard sets proportionality as the limit of punishment, tying it to the victim's rights and permitting restitution or mercy at the victim's choice.
missingStatements.declined: Proportional punishment and restitution is a narrow criminal-law detail.

missingStatements.text: Fraud and breach of contract should be treated as forms of aggression just as theft and violence are.
missingStatements.rationale: The tradition holds that force or fraud violates rights and Rothbard treats contract as a transfer of property title.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow libertarian legal doctrine; initiating-force-wrong already covers aggression.

notes: Anarcho-capitalists (Rothbard, Hoppe) and minarchists (Nozick) answer state-related statements differently, so those answers sit near 0. Immigration is contested: the party platform and Rothbard's property argument favour open movement while Hoppe's strand defends restriction. Intellectual property is split between those who reject patents and copyrights and those who accept some form.
